newsitem.title: JAPAN: Palladium lease rates jump on Russia supply delays.
newsitem.headline: Palladium lease rates jump on Russia supply delays.

text.p: Short-term palladium lease rates jumped during Asian hours on Wednesday, reflecting a tightening in the Zurich spot market as Russian exports to Japan were delayed further, traders said.
One-month lease rates soared to about 10 percent, compared with six percent on Tuesday and about three percent earlier this year.
Lease rates are what traders pay to borrow metal for a specific period of time, usually to fill immediate requirements.

"Market participants, who had expected a resumption of Russian exports in April, started to cover their short positions due to further delays in Russian exports to Japan," an official at a major bullion house said.
"The Zurich market has become tighter as someone is trying to squeeze the market," he added.
Earlier in the week, a Russian trade official in Tokyo said there would be no exports to Japan in April and possibly none in May.
The official also said that the Russian platinum group export agency, Almaz, did not know when Japan-Russia export contract talks, delayed since mid-December, might be held.

The sharp rise in palladium lease rates was also due in part to large short positions still held in yen-based Tokyo palladium futures by private investors, who are hoping prices will tumble once Russia's exports to Japan resume.

Japanese trade houses, who bought palladium futures from private investors and then sold palladium on the spot market in arbitrage trade, have been forced to borrow metal to cover their short spot positions, the traders said.

"The situation in the palladium market is now becoming quite serious," one bullion house official said. "We will be forced to buy metal in the spot market since we can no longer afford to borrow metal at such abnormally high lease rates."
Japanese traders said palladium prices were expected to rise further unless Russia resumed spot sales of the metal.
Palladium was fixed in London on Wednesday at $157.75 per ounce, a fresh 21-month high. Spot palladium was quoted around $145 per ounce at the end of March.
